title: Skip the 1 s publish deal diff when the ledger write count has not moved
body:
## Summary
Every idle 1 s tick the desktop actor's publish pass lists every deal and JSON-serializes each twice to diff it, even when nothing was written since the last pass.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/actor.rs:642 always publishes on a tick; publish() at crates/table-runtime/src/actor.rs:670 calls list_deals and at :682 serializes the old and new copy of every deal. A Deal is a pure projection of the ledger (read_deal in crates/table-ledger/src/repositories.rs), and the desktop has exactly one writer connection (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/native.rs:320; Book opens read-only), so Ledger::write_count (SQLite total_changes, crates/table-ledger/src/lib.rs:161) is a complete change signal for deals. Fixed: Published keeps the write count of its last successful deal diff and skips the diff when unchanged; attention and settings stay per tick (clock-driven).

## Flow
- idle wallet, 1 s tick -> publish -> list_deals (one statement since cccc62bb) + 2N serde_json::to_string -> zero events
- fix: Published.deals_at: Option<u64>; diff only when write_count != deals_at; set deals_at after a successful diff

## Expected impact
Desktop idle CPU drops by one whole-wallet decode plus 2N serializations per second. Could break: a deal change that does not move total_changes (none known: deal writes go through Ledger::write).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - the idle tick does no deal work when nothing was written
Before: 1 list_deals + 2N JSON serializations per idle second (code read; list_deals 4.1 ms at 500 deals after cccc62bb)
After: 0 per idle second (predicted; instrument = a cfg(test) deal_diffs counter beside publish_passes, a case in crates/table-runtime/src/publish_tests.rs)
Method: simulation - three walked cases (idle tick, tick after a deadline-default write, quiet read message); not built because actor.rs carries another session's uncommitted in-flight edits (veto 4)
Result: better
Gate: none

title: MCP server shutdown polls the actor's sender every 100 ms for the app's lifetime
body:
## Summary
The loopback MCP server's graceful-shutdown future wakes 10 times a second forever to check whether the actor's sender is gone.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/actor.rs:586-593 loops sender.upgrade().is_none() with a 100 ms sleep. The actor's run() ends when its receiver closes; a oneshot or Notify fired after run()'s loop gives the same shutdown with zero idle wakeups.

## Flow
- app idle -> 10 timer wakeups/s on the runtime
- fix: run() signals a oneshot on exit; with_graceful_shutdown awaits it

## Expected impact
Fewer idle wakeups (battery, timer coalescing). Could break: shutdown ordering, unchanged from today if the signal fires where the loop ends.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - zero idle wakeups for shutdown detection
Before: 10 wakeups/s (code read)
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: simulation - code walk; not built because actor.rs carries another session's in-flight edits (veto 4)
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Ledger writes pay rollback-journal fsyncs; WAL measured 4x cheaper per write
body:
## Summary
The ledger opens SQLite in the default rollback-journal mode, so every write transaction pays the journal create/fsync/delete cycle.

## Description
crates/table-ledger/src/lib.rs:76-78 sets foreign_keys, recursive_triggers and busy_timeout but no journal_mode. WAL with synchronous=FULL keeps per-commit durability and lets the read-only Book connection (crates/table-ledger/src/book.rs:197) read without blocking the writer. VACUUM INTO snapshots (crates/table-ledger/src/snapshot.rs:38) work unchanged under WAL; no production code copies the DB file raw (no fs::copy outside tests). Open points for the worker: -wal/-shm sidecars beside wallet.sqlite and house.sqlite3; a read-only Book open needs the -shm present (it is while the writer is open); tests that copy the raw file (crates/table-ledger/src/tests.rs:1208, :3272) may need a checkpoint first.

## Flow
- money step -> Ledger::write -> BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT -> journal fsyncs
- fix: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA synchronous=FULL in from_connection, a test pinning both, a checkpoint before any raw copy

## Expected impact
Every audited write (deals, envelopes, audit rows) gets cheaper on the desktop and on the 0.5-CPU house box. Could break: tooling or tests that copy the .sqlite file without its -wal.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - cheaper durable write transactions
Before: 2.30 / 2.39 ms per write txn (DELETE journal, synchronous=FULL)
After: 0.53 / 0.52 ms per write txn (WAL, synchronous=FULL)
Method: experiment - 300 BEGIN IMMEDIATE/INSERT/UPDATE/COMMIT txns on a temp file via Python sqlite3, two reps per mode, this machine; not the real Ledger, so the worker re-measures on table-ledger's own write path
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-ledger/src/lib.rs:76-78 (no journal_mode)
experiment: DELETE 2.30/2.39 ms, WAL 0.53/0.52 ms per txn
instrument: timing probe over Ledger writes on a temp file, both modes

title: Attention snapshot rebuilt from the whole ledger every second while idle
body:
## Summary
The 1 s publish pass rebuilds the attention stack from every deal and every counterparty, even when neither the ledger nor any deadline moved.

## Description
crates/table-runtime/src/dispatcher.rs:290 lists every deal (terminal ones included) and reads counterparty_list, then builds sources and a forecast every tick; the result is diffed as a JSON string in attention_event (crates/table-runtime/src/actor.rs). Attention is clock-dependent (deadline ladder, idle lock), so a write-count gate alone is wrong: the fix keeps the last sources and re-snapshots only when write_count moved or now crosses the next ladder boundary.

## Flow
- idle tick -> attention() -> list_deals + counterparty_list + per-deal attention_source -> snapshot -> serialize -> compare
- fix: cache sources by write_count; re-snapshot at the next ladder boundary

## Expected impact
Desktop idle CPU stops scaling with wallet size. Could break: a time-driven attention change missed if the boundary is wrong; ladder_tests and publish case 8 guard it.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - idle attention work bounded by changes, not wallet size
Before: 1 full deal list + counterparty list + N attention_source per second (code read)
After: 0 per second between boundaries (predicted)
Method: simulation - code walk of dispatcher.rs:276-306; not built: dispatcher.rs carries another session's in-flight edits and the boundary needs its own instrument
Result: better
Gate: none

title: ts-rs and its derive compile into every release build, including the house image
body:
## Summary
ts-rs is a normal dependency of table-core, table-attention, table-engine, table-proto and table-client, so its proc macro and 206 derive expansions compile into house-seller and the desktop release.

## Description
Bindings are generated by tests and a bin (crates/table-client/tests/bindings.rs), yet #[derive(ts_rs::TS)] is unconditional: 206 sites and 51 #[ts(...)] attributes across 34 files. cargo tree -p house-seller -e normal -i ts-rs shows it reaching the server through table-core, table-attention and rendezvous. Fix: a ts feature per crate, cfg_attr(feature = "ts", derive(TS)) and cfg_attr(feature = "ts", ts(...)), enabled by table-client's binding test and generator bin.

## Flow
- docker build -> cargo build --release -p house-seller -> compiles ts-rs-macros and TS impls for every IPC type
- fix: feature-gate, enable only where bindings are generated, assert the bindings are byte-identical

## Expected impact
Shorter house and desktop release builds and a smaller dependency surface. Could break: binding generation if a crate's feature is not enabled in the generator's graph.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer compile units in release builds
Before: ts-rs + ts-rs-macros + 206 derives in the house-seller release graph (cargo tree)
After: none in that graph (predicted); compile-time delta unmeasured
Method: simulation - cargo tree evidence; the timing needs cargo build --release --timings on both arms, which needs TABLE_HOUSE_RELEASE_JSON and two cold release builds
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
cargo tree -p house-seller -e normal -i ts-rs -> table-core, table-attention, rendezvous
grep derive(.*TS in crates: 206 sites in 34 files

title: CI's Rust legs cache nothing: 791 s Windows / 381 s Ubuntu cold on every push
body:
## Summary
Neither Rust leg of .github/workflows/ci.yml caches ~/.cargo or target/, so every push compiles the whole workspace from scratch, twice per OS (clippy, then test).

## Description
Last green main run (42077790978, 2026-11-05): rust (windows-latest) 791 s = clippy 205 s + test 532 s; rust (ubuntu-latest) 381 s = clippy 104 s + test 233 s. The pnpm side is cached (setup-node cache: pnpm, install 2-5 s). A keyed cache of ~/.cargo/registry, ~/.cargo/git and target/ (key: OS + Cargo.lock + rust-toolchain.toml) turns most pushes into incremental builds. Owner's choice: actions/cache (first-party, manual key) or a SHA-pinned Swatinem/rust-cache (new third-party trust, prunes target itself). Per ci-execution-trust, PR runs restore but do not save, so a branch cannot poison main's cache.

## Flow
- push -> 2 OS legs -> cold clippy + cold test
- fix: restore a cache before clippy; save on main only

## Expected impact
Wall-clock per push and runner minutes on both legs. Could break: a stale cache masking a dependency issue (--locked still checks the lock).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - CI wall-clock per push
Before: 791 s Windows, 381 s Ubuntu (run 42077790978)
After: unmeasured - needs a CI run with a warm cache
Method: gate - CI timings are the instrument; operator-only act: needs a push and a decision on which cache action to trust
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
gh run view 42077790978: rust (windows-latest) 791s [clippy 205s, test 532s]; rust (ubuntu-latest) 381s [clippy 104s, test 233s]
.github/workflows/ci.yml: no actions/cache, no rust-cache

title: Docker build installs a second Rust toolchain because rust-toolchain.toml says 1.97
body:
## Summary
The house image builds FROM rust:1.97-bookworm, but the context carries rust-toolchain.toml with channel "1.97", which rustup treats as a different toolchain from the image's 1.97.x, so an uncached build downloads a full toolchain plus clippy and rustfmt.

## Description
Dockerfile:1 pins the compiler by image tag; Dockerfile:3 COPY . . brings rust-toolchain.toml (channel = "1.97", components rustfmt, clippy). rustup names "1.97" and "1.97.1" as separate toolchains: this machine lists both 1.97-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and 1.97.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. Fix: add rust-toolchain.toml to .dockerignore (the image tag is the pin), or set ENV RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN to the image's toolchain.

## Flow
- deploy -> docker build -> cargo -> rustup reads rust-toolchain.toml -> installs 1.97 + rustfmt + clippy
- fix: one .dockerignore line

## Expected impact
Faster, less network-dependent house deploys. Could break: nothing at build while the image tag stays on 1.97.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - house image build time and download
Before: an extra toolchain install per uncached build (predicted from rustup naming shown locally)
After: none (predicted)
Method: probe - rustup toolchain list shows 1.97 and 1.97.1 as distinct toolchains; the docker build itself was not run (no Docker daemon on this machine)
Result: better
Gate: none (operator-only act: a docker build to confirm)
evidence:
rustup toolchain list:
  1.97-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (active)
  1.97.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
Dockerfile:1 FROM rust:1.97-bookworm
rust-toolchain.toml: channel = "1.97", components = [rustfmt, clippy]

title: Docker context ships the frontend, film and UAT trees the Rust build never reads
body:
## Summary
.dockerignore is a denylist that misses apps/desktop/client, film, uat, branding, scripts and *.mp4, so the context is 3.4x larger than the build needs and any frontend commit invalidates the COPY . . layer.

## Description
The house build reads Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, .cargo, crates/, services/, prompts/ (include_str in crates/table-core/src/agent.rs:572) and the apps/desktop/src-tauri manifest (workspace member). Tracked files in today's context: 1396 files, 16.69 MB; with an allowlist: 359 files, 4.87 MB. Locally the context also carries demo-film-latest.mp4 (62 MB), film/ (173 MB) and uat/ (64 MB). Paired with a dependency layer (cargo-chef or a BuildKit cache mount), a frontend-only commit would stop forcing a cold release build of ~220 crates.

## Flow
- docker build -> send context -> COPY . . -> any file change -> cold cargo build --release
- fix: allowlist .dockerignore (*, then !Cargo.toml !Cargo.lock !.cargo !crates !services !apps/desktop/src-tauri !prompts, then **/target), then a deps layer

## Expected impact
Smaller upload and fewer cold rebuilds per house deploy. Could break: the build if the allowlist misses an include_str path; a docker build is the only verifier.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - build context size and layer reuse
Before: 1396 tracked files / 16.69 MB (local adds ~300 MB of media)
After: 359 files / 4.87 MB
Method: experiment - node script over git ls-files applying both ignore lists; docker build not run (no daemon)
Result: better
Gate: none (operator-only act: a docker build to confirm)
evidence:
tracked context now 1396 files 16.69 MB; after 359 files 4.87 MB
du: demo-film-latest.mp4 62M, film 173M, uat 64M
Dockerfile:3 COPY . .
